body.heading: Where in the world is Japan?
paragraphs: Japan is a country in Eastern Asia, which is part of Asia. It is an island country, surrounded by sea.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Japan is Tokyo.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in Japan is Japanese.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Japan is the Japanese yen.

body.heading: How big is Japan?
paragraphs: Japan covers about 378,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about half the size of Türkiye.

body.heading: A fact to wow your friends
paragraphs: Japan has a high-speed railway system called the Shinkansen, known for its bullet trains. The fastest bullet trains whisk families between cities at up to 320 kilometres per hour.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Kyoto holds over a thousand temples — walk the vermilion gates of Fushimi Inari, the golden pavilion of Kinkaku-ji and the whispering Arashiyama bamboo grove.
Mount Fuji is Japan's beloved sacred mountain. Families view its perfect cone from Lake Kawaguchi, ride the Hakone ropeway, or climb it in summer season.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Japan on a map or globe. Which continent is it nearest to — and what sea or ocean surrounds it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?

takeaway: Japan in one breath: a country in Eastern Asia, capital Tokyo, where people speak Japanese and pay with the Japanese yen.
